title: Only reform
hookLine: Shu'ayb says: I want only reform, as far as I am able, and my success is from Allah (11:88)

lines: THE FIRST PAGE OF A THESIS.
MY SUCCESS COMES ONLY FROM GOD.
cards: A short line of Arabic sometimes sits on the first page of a Muslim student's thesis, or above the desk in a family shop: wa ma tawfiqi illa billah. My success comes only from God. It's from the Qur'an.
What's easy to miss is who said it first, and what kind of day he was having. It was Shu'ayb, the prophet of Madyan, the town with the crooked scales you met in al-A'raf. He was being mocked.
And the line was half of his answer.

teach.b: Madyan had sneered: Shu'ayb, does your prayer tell you how we should spend our own money? His answer in verse eighty-eight has three parts.
First, in paraphrase: I don't want to go behind your backs and do the very thing I'm forbidding you. No hidden deal, no double standard.

teach.h: ONLY REFORM, AS FAR AS I'M ABLE.
teach.b: Second, in Pickthall's translation: "I desire naught save reform so far as I am able." And third: my success comes only from God; in Him I trust, and to Him I turn. The key word is islah.

Its root, s-l-h, means to be sound, whole, working the way it should. The prophet Salih, two days ago, carries the same root in his name. The root also gives sulh, reconciliation, making peace between two people.
So islah is repair: of a scale, a market, a friendship. Notice what Shu'ayb doesn't claim. Not: I'll fix everything.
As far as I am able. And the results aren't his to own. Then Surah Hud keeps going, past the line that ends up on the walls.
Verse eighty-nine: don't let your quarrel with me push you into wrong.
Verse ninety: ask forgiveness; my Lord is merciful, loving, wadud.
And their answer, verse ninety-one: we don't understand much of what you say, and if it weren't for your clan, we'd have stoned you. Shu'ayb replies: is my clan more honored by you than God?
Even with threats on the table, the reformer stays honest, modest about his reach, and points past himself.

how: Some Muslims write or say wa ma tawfiqi illa billah, my success comes only from God, from 11:88, at the start of a book, a thesis or a new venture, and scholars cite Shu'ayb's words as a model for anyone working for reform.

o: repair, setting things right, making them whole
a punishment sent down on a corrupt town
a rebellion against a town's leaders

p: my success comes only from God

s: Shu'ayb promised to fix everything in Madyan
he said: only reform, as far as I am able, and my success comes from God.

games.q: you're Shu'ayb. your people say: if it weren't for your clan, we'd have stoned you. what do you answer?
o: then my clan will deal with you.
is my clan more honored by you than God?
games.why: is my clan more honored by you than God? he points past his family's protection to God (11:92).

practice: Think of one small thing in your world that isn't quite right: a wobbly chair, a bill that's wrong in your favor, a cold silence between two people you know.

Not the whole world, one thing, as far as you're able, and check Shu'ayb's first rule: do you ask of others what you don't do yourself? If you pray, you can say his words: my success comes only from God.

wordCard.voice: Islah. Reform, repair, setting things right, from the root s-l-h, to be sound and whole. Shu'ayb wanted only islah, as far as he was able. Today's word.
